'''Anatol Roshko''' (15 July 1923 – 23 January 2017) was a Canadian-born physicist and engineer who made fundamental contributions to [[fluid dynamics]] and the study of [[turbulence]]. He was the [[Theodore von Kármán]] Professor of [[Aeronautics]], [[Emeritus]], at the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Caltech Mourns the Passing of Anatol Roshko, 1923–2017|url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/caltech-mourns-passing-anatol-roshko-1923-2017-53690|access-date=2021-05-07|website=California Institute of Technology|date=23 January 2017 |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Roshko was born in [[Bellevue, Alberta]] in the Dominion of Canada in 1923. He completed his undergraduate education at the [[University of Alberta]], where he earned a [[B.Sc.]] degree in [[Engineering Physics]] in 1945. After a brief tour in the [[Royal Canadian Artillery]], he moved to Caltech's [[Guggenheim Aeronautical Laboratory]], where he earned an [[M.Sc.]] degree in 1947 and a [[Ph.D.]] in 1952. He studied under [[Hans W. Liepmann]] and wrote a thesis on turbulence in vortex wakes. As a graduate student, he conducted research through the [[National Advisory Committee on Aeronautics]] (NACA), the predecessor to [[NASA]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Aeronautics |first1=United States National Advisory Committee for |title=Annual Report of the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics |date=1954 |publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2GQiAQAAMAAJ&dq=anatol+roshko&pg=PA801 |access-date=13 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Roshko spent his career at Caltech, beginning as a research fellow in 1952 and a senior fellow in 1954. He was appointed assistant professor in 1958 and attained tenure in 1958 before becoming a full professor in 1962. Roshko was named von Kármán Professor in 1985 and retired in 1994. He served as director of the Guggenheim Aeronautical Laboratory (GALCIT) from 1985 to 1987.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Heppenheimer |first1=T. A. |title=Facing the Heat Barrier: A History of Hypersonics |date=2006 |publisher=NASA |isbn=978-1-4700-3267-8 |page=296 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=O0fNGTTuR5oC&dq=anatol+roshko&pg=PA254 |access-date=13 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

In the decades following 1952, he was regarded as a seminal fluid dynamics theorist, modeler, and experimentalist. Roshko is known for his contributions to gas dynamics and turbulence using high-speed imaging.<ref>{{cite book |title=Cornell Engineering Quarterly |date=1993 |publisher=College of Engineering, Cornell University |page=21 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oblaAAAAYAAJ&q=anatol+roshko |access-date=13 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> He co-authored the widely used textbook ''Elements of Gasdynamics'' with his former advisor, Hans W. Liepmann. He made influential research contributions to problems of [[flow separation]], bluff-body [[aerodynamics]], and the structure of turbulent shear flow.<ref name="Papamoschou">{{cite journal |last1=Papamoschou |first1=Dimitri |last2=Gharib |first2=Morteza |title=Anatol Roshko, 1923–2017 |journal=Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics |date=5 January 2020 |volume=52 |issue=1 |pages=1–18 |doi=10.1146/annurev-fluid-010719-060122 |bibcode=2020AnRFM..52....1P |s2cid=214008694 |language=en |issn=0066-4189|doi-access=free }}</ref> He also studied [[shock wave]]–[[boundary layer]] interactions using [[shock tube]] technology.<ref>{{cite web |title=Anatol Roshko |url=https://ame.usc.edu/seminars/keynote-lecture-series/anatol-roshko/ |website=USC Viterbi {{!}} Department of Aerospace & Mechanical Engineering |access-date=13 February 2026}}</ref>

Apart from scientific research, he was a consultant for the [[Office of Naval Research]] and companies including [[McDonnell Douglas]], [[Rockwell International]], and [[General Motors]]. In 1970, he helped organize the Wind Engineering Research Council and served on its executive board until 1983.<ref name="Papamoschou"/>

Roshko was an elected member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and [[National Academy of Engineering]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Memorial Tributes: Anatol Roshko |journal=National Academies |date=2022 |volume=24 |pages=298–301 |url=https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/26492/chapter/52#299 |access-date=13 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> He was a fellow of the [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics]] (AIAA), the [[American Physical Society]] (APS), the [[Canadian Aeronautics and Space Institute]], the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], and an Honorary Fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Papamoschou" />

He died in his home in [[Altadena, California]], on January 23, 2017, aged 93.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Anatol Roshko |url=https://www.nae.edu/CheckRobotPage.html?redirectUrl=/28649/Dr-Anatol-Roshko |access-date=2026-11-09 |website=www.nae.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-01-23 |title=Caltech Mourns the Passing of Anatol Roshko, 1923–2017 |url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/caltech-mourns-passing-anatol-roshko-1923-2017-53690 |access-date=2026-11-09 |website=California Institute of Technology |language=en}}</ref>
